title: LIVE CLOUD COVER — Great Lakes Basin Coverage
freshness: LIVE / CURRENT IR OBSERVATION (multi-satellite, honest timestamps)
noaa_source: GOES-19/18 ABI infrared + Himawari-9 infrared (via NASA GIBS) + Meteosat SEVIRI infrared imagery (via EUMETSAT EUMETView) + VIIRS daily polar supplement (via NASA GIBS)
product_name: GOES-19/18 ABI infrared + Himawari-9 infrared (via NASA GIBS) + Meteosat SEVIRI infrared imagery (via EUMETSAT EUMETView) + VIIRS daily polar supplement (via NASA GIBS)
variable: Infrared window brightness (GOES/Himawari BT in K, VIIRS BT in K, Meteosat grayscale imagery) -> white-cloud brightness + transparency. Not a cloud-cover percentage.
source_last_modified_utc: GOES-19 2026-11-12 13:10 UTC; GOES-18 2026-11-12 13:10 UTC; HIMAWARI-9 2026-11-12 12:30 UTC; METEOSAT-FES 2026-11-12 13:00 UTC; METEOSAT-IODC 2026-11-12 13:00 UTC; GDPS-TCC unknown
units: IR brightness (white=cold cloud tops; not a percentage)
spatial_resolution_source: multi-satellite IR: GOES-19/18 10.3um FD, Himawari-9 10.3um, Meteosat SEVIRI 10.8um, VIIRS I5 daily supplement; GOES full disks are inverse-georeferenced and resampled (no fixed-grid moire); polar |lat| 55-65 blend GDPS_15km_TotalCloudCover
missing_data_treatment: transparent = clear sky or no valid observation; never stretched or duplicated. Polar bands (|lat| ~55+ for the worldwide variants) blend the GDPS cloud-cover MODEL in place of single-channel IR, which cannot separate cold surfaces from cloud there; model values are labeled in provenance.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.
attribution: Data: US NOAA. This project is not endorsed by NOAA. See DATA_SOURCES.md for exact products and endpoints.
legend_scale_html: White = cloud tops (multi-satellite infrared, day + night; polar bands |lat| 55-65 blend the GDPS model cloud cover because single-channel IR there cannot separate cold ground/ice from cloud); transparent = clear sky or no satellite coverage. Infrared brightness, not a cloud-cover percentage.

na_bounds.note: Authoritative common geography for all three live layers. Every product bins its own source grid onto this exact canvas, so the three overlays align perfectly in Google Earth.
